Definition: probably for Latin aquila (an eagle); Akulas, an Israelite:--Aquila.
BiblicalUsage: Aquila is a Jewish tentmaker from Pontus, driven from Rome by Claudius, who meets Paul in Corinth and becomes his fellow worker.
TheologicalSignificance: I love that Aquila is remembered with his wife, in every mention. The two of them taught a great preacher, hosted a church, and risked their lives for Paul — and the work of the gospel has always run on people like them, whose names history nearly forgets.
RelatedEvents: Apollos Taught at Ephesus; Paul at Corinth
